questions.prompt: Why are the contrast rules for large text more forgiving?

options.text: Large text is only used for decorative purposes.
Large, thick letterforms provide more surface area for the eye to track.
Large text cannot be rendered in low-contrast colors.
Users automatically zoom out when reading large text.

questions.explanation: The physical weight and size of large text make it easier to resolve, lowering the need for high contrast.
questions.hint: Think about how physical size affects how easily the eye catches a shape.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Recognize how physical size impacts visual perception.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum contrast ratio for text that qualifies as large?
questions.explanation: Large text has a threshold of 3, lower than the 4.5 target for standard text.
questions.hint: It is the lower of the two standard thresholds.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify the 3 ratio threshold for large text.

questions.prompt: At what pixel size does bold text qualify as large in the research?
questions.explanation: The research gives 24 pixels in a regular weight or about 18.5 pixels in a bold weight.
questions.hint: Bold text requires fewer pixels than regular text to reach the size threshold.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Define the specific pixel sizes that qualify text as large.
